detail.title: WAKE✳︎ Research Synthesis and Notebook Updates
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes new research evidence across the active domains of objective records, record robustness, and scrambling, culminating in revised and new notebook documentation.

detail.title: Operational Frameworks for Objective Records
detail.summary: Objective reality in quantum systems emerges through environmental redundancy, where information about system states is broadcast into the environment. Independent observers can access this information via local measurements, consistent with the framework of Quantum Darwinism.
detail.reason: Notebook revised to incorporate Quantum Darwinism foundations and effective classicality definitions.

detail.title: Mechanisms of Objectivity: Quantum Darwinism and Redundancy
detail.summary: Robustness in quantum records arises from the redundancy of information stored in the environment. This redundancy allows multiple observers to measure different environment fractions and infer the same system state.
detail.reason: Notebook revised to reflect the distinction between environmental and usable redundancy.

detail.title: Divergence of Scrambling and Redundancy
detail.summary: Quantum scrambling, characterized by rapid information delocalization, often competes with the formation of redundant records. While scrambling tends to erase local information, the subsequent emergence of objective records suggests a complex trade-off between information spreading and environmental encoding.
detail.reason: New notebook created to synthesize literature on scrambling and redundancy.
